title: Autoloader subsystem (dynamic attributes)
description: Per-instance attributes of an autoloader: the service channels this loader accepts, the discovery table it uses to query its upstream ammo rack, and the crew query plus post multipliers of its human stage. A loader is both the provider for downstream launchers, the consumer of an upstream rack and the employer of the human stage, so all three live on the instance.

definition.description: Resource location of the subsystem model, pointing at the matching autoloader static attribute definition.

ammo_discovery_inputs.description: Service channels this loader accepts. Downstream launchers run a read-only discovery on these channels and find this loader. Channels express a service class only (e.g. ammo_57mm) and carry no business signals.

ammo_discovery_targets.description: Upstream query table: service channel to target names. First-party content points at the matching rack subsystem by name, so the scope covers exactly that pair. The upstream query accepts stock holders only; loaders never accept other loaders, so a mechanical chain cannot cycle.

reload_operator_discovery_targets.description: Crew query table of the human stage: crew channel to target names. The usual form is {"crew.reload.loader": ["local"]} — local is every SubPart of the part, so a seat is found as soon as it declares the same channel in its own reload_operator_discovery_inputs; two turrets built in two parts stay isolated by local. Only meaningful when the model configures human_reload_time. Channels are handshakes for discovery only and carry no loading commands.

reload_operator_time_multipliers.description: Post multipliers P: crew channel to multiplier, e.g. {"crew.reload.loader": 1.0, "crew.reload.gunner": 2.0}. They belong to the relation between this loader and that seat, not to the seat as a global ability; the same seat may carry another multiplier when serving another weapon. Unlisted channels count as 1.0 and values must be finite and positive. When several channels reach the same seat, the lowest multiplier among them applies: a seat yields one candidate and multipliers never add up.
